To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a patient with a combined JP‐HHT phenotype has a translocation disrupting the gene SMAD4, which was confirmed by NGS and Sanger sequencing.
a chromosomal translocation involving SMAD4 was found in a JP‐HHT patient.

a) a chromosomal translocation involving the SMAD4 locus was found to be responsible for JP-HHT; and that b) the translocation resulted in a truncated, nonfunctional protein product, which is consistent with the known function of the SMAD4 protein in the canonical TGF-β signaling pathway.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery of the genetic cause of a patient with the combined JP‐HHT phenotype.
the clinical presentation, molecular genetic findings, and management of this rare disease entity.
the discovery of a novel variant of JP‐HHT in a patient with a complex phenotype.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SMAD4 translocation is a rare cause of JP‐HHT.
this is a case of JPS and HHT with a translocation involving the SMAD4 locus.
this translocation is not only a rare cause of JP‐HHT, but also a rare event in the human genome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the patient presented with a rare JP‐HHT variant, which was identified using a NGS approach.
the SMAD4 germline variant is a cause of the combined phenotype of JPS and HHT.
we report a transposition event involving SMAD5 and SMAD4 resulting a combined phenotype of Juvenille Polyposis syndrome and Hemorrhagic Telagiectasia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SMAD4 is a rare but important cause of JP‐HHT, and that the presence of a germline SMAD4 variant in a patient presenting with HHT should be investigated with a chromosomal analysis.
the SMAD4 variant should be considered as a cause of JP‐HHT in cases where NGS techniques fail to identify a causative sequence variant in HHT.
NGS techniques can be used to identify germline variants that result in the combined phenotype JP‐HHT, which may lead to the identification of additional genes that are involved in this disease.
